# contrast.plot_contrasts.plot_contrasts { #fmrimod.contrast.plot_contrasts.plot_contrasts }

```python
plot_contrasts(
    x,
    absolute_limits=False,
    rotate_x_text=True,
    scale_mode='auto',
    figsize=None,
)
```

Plot contrast weights as a heatmap.

Dispatches on ``x``: an ``EventModel`` (its contrasts, labelled from its
columns, with standard errors from its design) or a dict mapping
contrast names to weight vectors or ``p x k`` matrices (F-contrasts).

## Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name            | Type                                     | Description                                                                                                                | Default    |
|-----------------|------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------|
| x               | EventModel or dict                       |                                                                                                                            | _required_ |
| absolute_limits | bool                                     | Fix the fill at [-1, 1] (or [0, 1] one-sided) instead of the largest absolute weight.                                      | `False`    |
| rotate_x_text   | bool                                     | Angle column labels when they would overlap.                                                                               | `True`     |
| scale_mode      | (\'auto\', \'diverging\', \'one_sided\') | ``"auto"`` and ``"diverging"`` are symmetric about 0; ``"one_sided"`` is a neutral-to-warm scale for non-negative weights. | `"auto"`   |
| figsize         | (float, float)                           |                                                                                                                            | `None`     |

## Notes {.doc-section .doc-section-notes}

The implementations also take ``annotate``, ``title``, ``subtitle``,
``caption`` and ``ax``; the dict one also ``labels`` (column labels)
and ``design`` (a model or design matrix, enabling the SE column).

## Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type                     | Description   |
|--------|--------------------------|---------------|
|        | matplotlib.figure.Figure |               |
